title: Incident comms wargame scripts and status framing
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight, exercise-first runbook focused on incident communications: templated status page entries, customer-facing messages, and an internal war-room checklist. It is intended for tabletop wargames and as a quickstart for on-call engineers who need to stand up effective comms under pressure.

Scope and assumptions:
- Covers hosted API and Dedicated connectivity incidents (latency, partial degradation, regional outage).
- Emphasizes speed and clarity over exhaustive technical detail for the first 60 minutes.
- Roles referenced assume a primary on-call SRE, an engineering responder, and a communications lead (CS/SRE hybrid).

Key roles and responsibilities (one-liners):
- Bridge Lead: owns the bridge, coordinates triage, assigns actions.
- Communications Lead: drafts status page + customer notes, approves cadence.
- Engineering Responder: collects logs, runs mitigation playbooks, applies rollback if needed.
- CS Liaison: surfaces affected enterprise customers and drafts personalized outreach.
- Postmortem Owner: collates timeline, RCA, and follow-up actions.

Immediate (first 15 minutes) war-room checklist:
- [ ] Open or confirm incident ticket (JIRA key) and set severity label.
- [ ] Start the incident bridge and pin it in #sre-oncall.
- [ ] Assign Bridge Lead and Communications Lead.
- [ ] Publish initial status page entry (short, factual).
- [ ] Identify customer-impacting services and top affected regions.
- [ ] Capture key metrics: error rate, p95 latency, throughput, GPU utilization, queue depth.
- [ ] Turn on any safe capacity/fallback (route to secondary region / scale up critical pools).
- [ ] Notify CS for high-value customers and prepare personalized comms.

Status page templates (copy-paste friendly)
1) Severity: Partial degradation (customers see increased latency or token errors, no full outage)
- Title: "Reduced generation throughput for model-serving in <region>"
- Impact: "Customers may experience slower response times or intermittent token errors for some requests. Core routing and authentication are unaffected."
- Status: "Identified — Mitigation in progress"
- Started: "<YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC>"
- Next update: "<in 15–30 minutes>"
- Mitigation: "Traffic is being routed to warmed standby pools and autoscaling thresholds temporarily increased."
- Customer action: "No action required; we will post updates and follow-up with impacted accounts."

2) Severity: Regional outage (major impact to all requests in a region)
- Title: "Service disruption affecting model inference in <region>"
- Impact: "All requests routed through <region> may fail or time out. Customers in this region may see errors or cannot submit inference jobs."
- Status: "Investigating — fallback and routing tests underway"
- Started: "<YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC>"
- Expected resolution: "Investigating; estimated next update within 30 minutes"
- Mitigation: "Failover to alternate region enabled for eligible accounts; manual failover instructions provided to CS for enterprise requests."
- Customer action: "If you require immediate continuity, please contact support and request routing to <alternate-region>."

3) Severity: Degradation with partial data exposure risk (rare, security-related)
- Title: "Potential data exposure for requests routed through <component>"
- Impact: "We are investigating a possible data confidentiality issue affecting a subset of requests. We have isolated the affected component."
- Status: "Mitigating — component isolated, investigation ongoing"
- Started: "<YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC>"
- Next update: "<within 60 minutes>"
- Mitigation: "Isolated node groups and disabled diagnostic collection. Full audit later."
- Customer action: "We will reach out directly to potentially affected customers with more details once confirmed."

Customer-facing templates (email / ticket update)
A) Initial short notice (use within 10–20m of detection)
Subject: "Service disruption affecting inference in <region>"
Hi <Customer Name>,
We detected a service disruption impacting inference requests routed through <region>. Our SRE team is investigating and we have activated mitigation steps. You may see increased latency or errors for some requests. We’ll post updates on our status page (link) and follow up directly if your workspace is affected.
Estimated next update: <time>
Sincerely,
The Redwood Inference SRE team

B) Follow-up / mitigation update (when mitigation in place)
Subject: "Update: mitigation in place for inference disruption in <region>"
Hi <Customer Name>,
We’ve implemented routing changes that should restore most customer traffic to healthy pools. If you continue to experience issues, please reply to this message and include request IDs or timestamps. We’ll keep monitoring and provide a resolution note when the incident is closed.
Thanks for your patience.

C) Resolution + RCA summary (post-incident)
Subject: "Resolved: inference disruption in <region> — root cause and next steps"
Hi <Customer Name>,
The incident affecting inference in <region> has been resolved as of <time>. Root cause: <brief summary — e.g., misrouted kernel selection combined with high queue buildup>. Actions taken: <list mitigations>. Customer impact: <who/what was affected>. Preventative measures: <what we will change>. If you’d like a dedicated walkthrough, please let us know and we’ll schedule a call.
Apologies for the disruption — we know reliability matters and we’re investing to prevent recurrence.

Internal escalation matrix (times are guidelines)
- 0–5m: On-call detects issue, opens ticket, posts brief to #sre-oncall.
- 5–15m: Bridge Lead + Comm Lead assigned; status page initial entry published.
- 15–30m: If no clear mitigation, escalate to SRE manager + infra eng lead.
- 30–60m: If customer-impacting and unresolved, notify broader GTM (CS ops, account execs).
- >60m: Consider executive-level updates if top-tier accounts affected.

Wargame scripts (tabletop scenarios to practice comms)
Scenario A: Intermittent p95 spike for hosted API in us-east-1
- Inject: Simulate a sustained p95 latency increase of 2x for 30m.
- Objectives: Practice quick classification (degradation vs outage), publish status page, test personalized CS outreach, exercise temporary routing to warmed pools.
- Exercise steps: 1) on-call posts initial status; 2) comms lead drafts customer email; 3) CS liaison prepares account list for high-value customers; 4) engineering responder toggles routing to standby pools; 5) post-event debrief to capture timings.

Scenario B: Dedicated pool crash causing tokens to truncate for some customers
- Inject: Simulate GPU driver OOM leading to job truncation for reserved pools.
- Objectives: Practice enterprise comms, coordinate account-level mitigation (move to alternate dedicated pool), test crediting process for SLOs.

Scenario C: Third-party auth outage prevents token exchange (external dependency)
- Inject: OAuth provider returns 502 for 15 minutes.
- Objectives: Practice cross-team comms with security/ops, craft language to indicate external dependency, trigger CS outreach and support-scripting.

Communication quality metrics (what to measure after each incident/wargame)
- Time-to-first-comm (target < 10 minutes)
- Frequency of updates versus promised cadence (missed updates count)
- Customer-reported incidents vs inferred impact (signal quality)
- CS escalations and enterprise outreach latency
- Post-incident NPS/sentiment if collected for major outages

Post-incident follow-up checklist:
- [ ] Close incident ticket with final timeline and key artifacts (logs, dashboards, traces).
- [ ] Publish RCA and link from status page entry.
- [ ] Quantify customer impact (accounts, duration, SLOs affected).
- [ ] Issue SLO credits where applicable and notify CS billing.
- [ ] Add communication lessons to shared template library and update this doc.
- [ ] Schedule a blameless postmortem within 7 business days and assign Postmortem Owner.

Notes & tips:
- Keep the first status page post short and concrete: state the observable symptom, scope (who/where), and what you’re doing. Avoid speculation.
- Use a tone matrix: more transparency for enterprise customers and regulators; concise public posts for general users.
- For wargames, simulate noise: ask participants to inject Slack pings and account-owner requests to practice prioritization.
- Maintain a one-line summary at the top of each status page update for quick skimming.

Appendix: Quick copy snippets (for Slack/Status/Ticket)
- Slack short: "INC-XXXX: investigating increased inference errors in <region>. Bridge: <link>. Status page: <link>. Comm lead: @<name>."
- Ticket short: "Summary: Increased inference errors (p95 spike) in <region>. Impact: partial degradation. Bridge link: <link>."

End of draft.
This file is intended to be used in tabletop drills and as a starting template for on-call comms. Please leave edits inline and push changes to the consolidated SRE playbook after post-wargame updates.
